basis: Inherited PRNP-related neurodegeneration causes chorea, dementia and progressive neurologic dysfunction.
Chylomicron metabolism disorder; pancreatitis and steatosis are separate complications. Lipemia retinalis, xanthomas and organ enlargement alone do not establish functional damage.
Defining hypertriglyceridemia and hepatic steatosis, with fibrosis and elevated liver enzymes; splenomegaly alone does not establish blood-organ dysfunction.
Germ cell tumor arising in the lung.
Isolated congenital fusion and duplication of digits.
Mitochondrial metabolic encephalopathy; pigmentary retinopathy occurs in 30-79%. Cardiomyopathy, renal abnormalities and hearing loss are each occasional.
Defining skeletal and hand malformations with joint hypermobility; facial, palatal and ear dysmorphism alone does not establish additional organ dysfunction.
Inflammation of the orbital Tenon capsule; infectious or autoimmune causation is not specified.
Skeletal dysplasia and defective dental enamel/tooth development jointly define the syndrome; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Neurodevelopmental disorder of speech motor planning and language; oromotor apraxia does not establish intrinsic oral tissue disease.
Alzheimer neurodegeneration with dementia.
Carcinoma originates in ethmoid sinus mucosa; paranasal sinuses belong to the pulmonary axis.
Fungal infection of the meninges.
Soft-tissue sarcoma typically involving extremity fascia and tendon-associated tissues; dermal/subcutaneous origin varies across subtypes.
Developmental brain disorder with intellectual disability, epilepsy and movement abnormalities; hypotonia and feeding difficulty do not establish separate organ damage.
Spastic paraplegia and Paget bone disease jointly define the syndrome; weakness is neuropathic, with no reported primary myopathy.
Defined functional intestinal disorder with abdominal pain and altered bowel habits.
Inherited platelet deficiency; additional organ disease is subtype-specific rather than shared across the umbrella.
Congenital absence or hypoplasia of the ulna with associated limb and joint abnormalities.
Melanoma originating in the skin.
Periosteal inflammation and cortical new bone formation define the disease; associated soft-tissue swelling is transient, without established lasting skin damage.
Unilateral congenital duplication and fusion of digits.
Spinal neural/meningeal malformation with a stalk-containing meningocele and the vertebral closure defect of spina bifida cystica.
Isolated congenital partial absence of the cerebellar vermis.
Phosphate-regulation disorder with subcutaneous calcific masses; hyperostosis reported in 2/2 patients supports skeletal involvement. Renal and vascular damage frequencies are unspecified.
